review_notes:
I reviewed all 93 lines of the file. It declares only two theorems and no definitions, structures, abbreviations, instances or attributes.

- `sum_selected_cells_le_overlap` (lines 12–28) is an inequality for double sums weighted by how many windows overlap each cell.
- `manuscript_geometric_residue_energy` (lines 30–89) is an existential inequality with a filter condition, built from published-input hypotheses.

Both conclusions are `≤` statements with side hypotheses (nonnegativity, overlap bounds, analytic inputs). They are not rewrite rules, so neither one is a sensible candidate for `@[simp]`. The file adds no definitions, so there are no missing unfolding or characterization lemmas to suggest. A Grep over `lean/` found only internal uses of the two theorems. The second theorem is used by `Probability/GeometricHistogramErrors.lean` through `obtain`, not through simp.

The simplifier calls inside proofs (`simp` after `rw [← sum_filter]`, `simp_rw [he]`, `dsimp [w]`, `simpa using Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le`, `simpa only [w, Fintype.sum_prod_type]`) are local proof tactics. They use only existing Mathlib or local rules and do not create or change any simp interface. Definitions such as `manuscriptResidueEnergy`, `histogramWindowCells` and `channelMesh` live in other files, so their simp interfaces are outside this review. This file has nothing to which the simp-interface rubric meaningfully applies.
